title: Request Account Request
description: The single account write (experimental, account.requests). Open an account (brand and operator: the seller finds an existing one or creates one) or change one (account_id plus the attributes to change), possibly after human review on either side. Every write is a request with the same lifecycle. Experimental in 3.3 (#8280): sellers implementing this task MUST list account.requests in experimental_features. Retries are safe through idempotency_key; deduplicating separate requests for the same advertiser is seller discretion, with non-normative guidance in the task docs. Send either account_id, or brand and operator; sellers enforce this at runtime so the MCP input schema stays a plain root object, and reject a request carrying both, or neither, with INVALID_REQUEST. With account_id, every other field present is a requested change, validated as when the account opens: brand.domain and brand.brand_id must equal the account's (a different brand is a different account, INVALID_REQUEST), currency and timezone changes MAY be refused with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, and sandbox never changes.
x-tool-summary: Request an advertiser account: the seller matches an existing account or creates one, possibly after human review.

idempotency_key.description: Client-generated key that makes retries of this call safe, with the standard replay semantics. A replayed key returns the original request; a new key is a new request. Use a fresh UUID v4 for each logical call.

account_id.description: Change, or select, an existing account. With other fields present, the request changes those attributes on this account; the account keeps its account_id, media buys, and history. With no other fields, it selects the account: a candidate from an ambiguous request, or, on a platform that owns its account namespace, an account the caller's credential does not reach yet. For an account_id the caller cannot reach, the seller MUST answer the same way whether or not the account exists: either always rejected with ACCOUNT_NOT_FOUND, or, for sellers that support access requests, always in_review with waiting_on: buyer and kind: grant. Mutually exclusive with operator; brand is allowed only to change countries.

revision.description: Guard when changing an account (with account_id): the account revision the change is based on. Required when the change touches billing, billing_entity, or payment_terms, because a lost update there costs money; optional for other changes. Sellers enforce this at runtime and reject a money change without revision with INVALID_REQUEST. A stale revision fails the call with CONFLICT and changes nothing. Read it from list_accounts.

brand.description: Advertiser identity. Required to open an account. Sellers matching on brand use domain and brand_id; countries is an attribute. With account_id, send brand only to change countries; domain and brand_id must equal the account's.

operator.description: Domain of the entity operating on the brand's behalf. When the brand operates directly, the brand's domain. The seller verifies it against the brand's authorized_operators and, where grants are supported, the operator's grant to the calling agent. Required unless account_id is sent.

operator_unit.description: Optional operator-owned business unit or seat. An account attribute; name is display metadata.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency for a currency-bound advertiser object, as in sync_accounts. An account attribute set when the account opens.

timezone.description: Buyer-selected timezone when the seller declares account_fixed, buyer_selected timezones, as in sync_accounts. An account attribute set when the account opens.

sandbox.description: Request a sandbox account. An account attribute: a sandbox request does not match a production account.

billing.description: Requested invoiced party. A requested term, not account identity. The seller accepts it exactly or rejects the request; billing is never silently remapped.

billing_entity.description: Requested business entity for the invoiced party. A requested term, not account identity. Bank details are write-only.

payment_terms.description: Requested payment terms. A requested term, not account identity. The seller accepts them or rejects the request.

examples.description: Agency requests an operator-billed account for one advertiser
